moduleTitle: Managing and analyzing test results in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Describe how to debug tests during runtime by stopping, pausing, or stepping through them to identify issues efficiently.
Explain the process of organizing and filtering test results with result labels.
Articulate the process of tagging failed runs with failure types to capture valuable insights and improve test analysis.

elements.description: Local debug mode supports Pause/Continue, stepping and breakpoints. Pause stops at the nearest step boundary, not an arbitrary instant inside any action. Local playback without debugging does not pause at breakpoints; remote grid execution is not this local debug mode.

Continue/Play resumes a paused run from the current location, unlike Rerun, which restarts. Distinguish manual breakpoints from temporary virtual debug locations rather than promising every breakpoint marker remains unchanged.

Play from here starts after the selected arrow. Establish earlier required state, such as authentication and variables; skipping setup can cause failure. This is partial debugging, not full-flow coverage.

elements.text: This is the same debugging toolkit covered in more depth in the 'Debugging test cases' and 'Streamlining Testing and Debugging' modules — this course frames it specifically as part of the broader 'managing and analyzing results' workflow.

bulletPoints: Use local debug mode for pause/continue, stepping and breakpoints.
Pause is at a step boundary; Continue differs from restarting with Rerun.
Play from here needs the required prior state and does not establish whole-flow coverage.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Organizing and filtering with Result labels

elements.description: Free-text labels attached to a run — distinct from the Labels applied to tests in the Test Library. Result labels are commonly used to record things like which application environment was tested, which application version was tested, or which user/system executed the run (examples: 'nightly-scheduler', 'v1.42.34', 'Jenkins', 'Staging').

elements.term: Adding and filtering by result labels
elements.description: Add remote-run result labels with CLI --result-label or Scheduler Advanced Options. Each label has a 250-character maximum. Run pages support filtering; test-definition Labels are a separate selection/organization mechanism.

bulletPoints: Result labels ≠ Test Library labels — they tag a RUN, not a test definition.
Common uses: environment, application version, or the user/system (Jenkins, a scheduler) that triggered the run.
CLI and Scheduler add remote-run labels; these do not replace test-definition Labels.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Tagging failed runs with failure types

elements.description: Tag remote-run failures using the documented categories: Bug in app, Environment issue, Invalid test data, Test design or Other. These human-selected cause categories are distinct from engine errors such as Element not found or JavaScript Error.

Once failures are tagged, the failure-type filter can show only the runs tagged with a specific reason, and the Reports view's donut chart shows the percentage distribution of failure types (each tag's share of total runs, alongside its change vs. the previous period) — turning individual failures into a trend you can act on. Clicking a failure tag jumps straight to the Test Runs screen, pre-filtered to every run tagged with that type.

elements.text: Tagging does not repair the defect. With a configured tracker connection, the same dialog can link an existing issue or create/publish a new one, so separate manual re-entry is not universally required.

bulletPoints: Tagging a failed run with a failure type turns it into filterable, reportable data.
Reports' donut chart shows the % distribution of failure types over a period, revealing trends.
Clicking a failure tag jumps to the Test Runs screen filtered to that type.
Tagging does not fix defects; a configured tracker can receive a linked or newly published issue.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming Run Test after a breakpoint restarts the whole test
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting clicking Play/Run Test after a paused breakpoint to start the test over from step one.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Continue a paused local debug run from its current location; use Rerun to restart. Distinguish manual and virtual breakpoint behavior.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing Result labels with Test Library labels
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming a label applied to a run and a label applied to a test in the Test Library are the same mechanism.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Result labels tag a specific RUN (environment, version, triggering system); Test Library labels tag a TEST definition. They're filtered and used in different places.

examPitfalls.title: Treating failure-type tagging as an automated fix
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming tagging a failed run somehow resolves the underlying issue or removes the need to file a bug.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Investigate the cause and choose the appropriate tag. With tracker integration, link or publish an issue through the tagging workflow; the tag itself does not remediate the defect.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A local debug run is paused at a step boundary. What does Play/Continue do, as distinct from Rerun?

options.text: The test will skip to the next step.
The test will continue running from the breakpoint.

practiceQuiz.hint: It resumes exactly where it left off.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Play/Continue resumes the paused run from its current location. Rerun restarts; local playback without debugging does not pause at breakpoints.

optionExplanations.A: Continue does not mean Stop Run.
optionExplanations.B: It resumes from the current debug location, not intentionally skipping an unexecuted step.
optionExplanations.C: Continuing is not the command to remove a manual breakpoint.
optionExplanations.D: Continue resumes the paused run rather than restarting.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why would you use multiple result labels when executing tests in Testim?

options.text: To reduce the number of test cases executed.
To reduce the execution time for tests.
To ensure test results are archived correctly.
To track test execution across different environments.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think environment, version, and the system that triggered the run.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Result labels are commonly used to record things like which application environment or version was tested, or which user/system triggered the run — letting you track and filter execution across those different environments, not to reduce test count, execution time, or handle archiving.

optionExplanations.A: Result labels organize run metadata rather than reduce selected tests.
optionExplanations.B: Labels do not guarantee faster execution.
optionExplanations.C: Labels are not a retention/archive guarantee.
optionExplanations.D: They allow environment/version/source metadata to be tracked and filtered.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO are analysis benefits of tagging remote-run failures, distinct from repairing the defect or configuring tracker integration?

options.text: Ability to filter tests by failure type over a time period
Seeing the percentage of failures by type in reports
Eliminating the need to manually log defects

practiceQuiz.hint: It's an analysis/filtering aid, not an automated fix.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Tags support failure-type filtering and reporting. They do not automatically repair tests; tracker integration can link/create an issue but is separate from the analysis benefit.

optionExplanations.A: Tagged runs can be filtered over a selected period.
optionExplanations.B: A category tag does not repair the failing code or application.
optionExplanations.C: Reports can show distributions of selected cause categories.
optionExplanations.D: Tagging alone is not universal defect logging; tracker connection and publish actions remain separate.

quickRecap.value: Continue resumes a paused local debug run; Rerun starts over.
Starts after a selected arrow; prior dependencies must be established.
Remote-run metadata via CLI/Scheduler; up to 250 characters per label, distinct from test-definition labels.
Categorizes a failed run — enables filtering by type and % distribution in Reports; not an auto-fix.
